requirement:
The harness MUST record the sources it supplies to the model, including
mandatory inputs, additional reads, and selected search dependencies under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.finish_search.inputs`, using the evidence input formats
defined by {cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs`,
{cite}`requirements.ci.requirements_inputs`, and
{cite}`requirements.definitions.inputs`. The harness MUST create these records
itself so ordinary evidence validation can check them later.
rationale:
The reviewed tests adequately cover `requirements.authoring.delivered_inputs`. I derived four obligations from the requirement and mapped each to tests. I did not request implementation source.

**1. Mandatory inputs are recorded.**
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files]` runs six determination, evidence-file and verbose combinations. Each time it asserts that the evidence contains a requirements input for the subject, a definition input (`terms.readiness`), and outline inputs for `src/lib.rs`.
- The same test checks that outline inputs have exactly the keys `file`, `hash` and `item`, with no source text.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free]` asserts the mandatory `fn[ready_test]` outline input and the definition input. It also runs `validate_repository` to show the recorded evidence validates under ordinary evidence validation.
- `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[declaration_text_reaches_the_model_redacted]` checks that the recorded inputs match the delivered requirements and definition inputs, which cover the requirements and definition formats.

**2. Additional reads are recorded.**
- `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms]` covers item reads and line-range reads, including reads that run to end of file. It also covers definition and requirements reads and the terms they deliver. It asserts that nothing is recorded until `record_inputs` is called and that repeated delivery is deduplicated.
- `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[line_range_reads_record_the_innermost_covering_nodes]` checks that recorded outline inputs are exactly the `outline_input` values, with no `text` or `line_start` fields. It covers nested and plain-text files.
- Failed reads, `list_files` and unfinished searches add no inputs. The assertions are in the CLI test above (`absent.txt`, the `list_files` origin, and the `ripgrep` snippets not appearing as inputs). `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[implementation_discovery_has_no_text_or_evidence_until_the_model_requests_a_read]` adds that `references` results record nothing.

**3. Selected search dependencies are recorded.**
- `src/authoring/searches.rs#fn[selected_dependencies_keep_the_delivered_hash_and_accumulate_without_reads]` selects tag "1", with a duplicate, from a search. It asserts that the input equals the originally delivered `outline_input`, so the delivered hash is kept even after the file changes. It also asserts that unselected tags are not recorded, that selections accumulate across calls, and that a separate read of the same item is deduplicated.
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[a_helper_used_only_through_a_search_snippet_invalidates_saved_evidence_when_weakened]` shows an item selected from a ripgrep snippet becomes a recorded hash-only input. It also shows an unrelated item is not recorded and that no `habeas` call was needed.

**4. Only delivered material is recorded, and the harness creates the records.**
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[only_inputs_on_delivered_pages_are_recorded]` and `src/authoring/pages.rs#fn[paged_inputs_carry_their_definitions_and_deliver_only_their_own_inputs]` check that only entries on delivered pages are recorded. Undelivered later entries are absent. Each page's inputs and definitions equal exactly what it delivers.
- `src/authoring/sdk.rs#fn[confirmed_evidence_retains_reads_from_both_assessments_and_the_verifier]` shows reads from several assessments are retained as dependencies.
- The model supplies only tool arguments, and the harness builds the records. The tests above compare the recorded inputs to inputs the harness derives itself (`outline_input`, `outline_inputs_for_lines`).

The input formats themselves are cited requirements, so their validation is out of scope here. The tests do exercise the formats the harness records, as shown above.

I found no gaps and there are no acknowledgments to weigh.

text: :::{req} delivered_inputs
The harness MUST record the sources it supplies to the model, including
mandatory inputs, additional reads, and selected search dependencies under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.finish_search.inputs`, using the evidence input formats
defined by {cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs`,
{cite}`requirements.ci.requirements_inputs`, and
{cite}`requirements.definitions.inputs`. The harness MUST create these records
itself so ordinary evidence validation can check them later.
:::{req} finish_search.inputs
For each tag selected by a valid `finish_search` call, the harness MUST record
its `file`, `item`, and structural hash as an outline input under
{cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs` before acknowledging that call.
:::{req} outline_inputs
For an outline input, Habeas MUST parse `file` with its language's grammar under
{cite}`requirements.references.outlines` and resolve `item` to exactly one
outline node under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. It MUST
compare `hash` with the node's current structural hash under
{cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. It MUST derive the node's
inclusive line range, including attached comments and attributes, during
validation for display and reference coverage. Moving the node, editing other
nodes, or editing comments its profile does not hash MUST NOT invalidate the
input. Habeas MUST report a missing file, unsupported language, parse failure,
invalid or ambiguous selector, or changed hash.
:::{req} requirements_inputs

For a requirements input, `requirements` MUST be a {term}`requirements.references.definition_selection`, and Habeas MUST match it against all defined requirements and named examples. It MUST recompute the matches during validation, sort their full names, and compare them with `matches`. It MUST take each match's complete raw fenced declaration, including its opening and closing lines, concatenate those declarations in full-name order with one blank line between them, and compare the resulting raw lines with `text`. It MUST retain every match's current source file and inclusive line range for display and reference coverage. A selection matching no definitions MUST be invalid. Adding, removing, renaming, or changing a matched definition MUST invalidate the stored input; moving an unchanged declaration within the book MUST NOT. Errors MUST identify the selection and affected definitions when available.
:::{req} inputs

Evidence inputs MAY have a definition form containing exactly `definition` and `text`. `definition` MUST identify one named definition; `text` MUST contain its complete raw fenced declaration as source lines, including its phrase option and explanatory body.

Validation MUST reject missing definitions and changed snapshot text, identifying the definition and showing a compact diff when available. Moving an unchanged definition within its chapter MUST NOT invalidate its snapshot. Evidence displays MUST show the definition name, current source location, and recorded text.
:::{definition} definition_selection
:phrase: definition selection
A full requirement or example name, or a definition glob, identifying the
requirements and named examples it matches under
{cite}`requirements.references.definition_globs`. A name without `*` selects
exactly that definition.
